title: Philokalia, Greek (Athens 1893)
author: Nikodimos & Makarios (eds)
description: The Philokalia (Philokalia ton Ieron Neptikon, 'Love of the Beautiful of the Holy Watchful Fathers'), compiled by St Nikodimos of the Holy Mountain and St Makarios of Corinth, here in the Greek edition published in Athens in 1893 (the original was printed in Venice in 1782). It is a vast anthology of texts written between the fourth and fifteenth centuries by spiritual masters of the Orthodox tradition, among them Evagrius Ponticus, John Cassian, Mark the Ascetic, Diadochos of Photiki, Maximus the Confessor, Hesychios, Philotheos of Sinai, Peter of Damascus, Symeon the New Theologian, Nikitas Stithatos, Gregory of Sinai and Gregory Palamas. Its theme is watchfulness (nepsis), the guarding of the heart, the struggle with passions and thoughts, and continual prayer, especially the Jesus Prayer, leading to stillness (hesychia), the vision of divine light and deification (theosis). Translated into Slavonic and Russian, it sparked a spiritual revival and remains the central text of hesychasm.
